my docker build keeps failing and I have no idea why. it worked yesterday

Can you paste the last 20 or so lines of the output, and tell me what changed since yesterday (even small things)?

nothing changed I think?? here's the error:

 => ERROR [builder 4/7] RUN npm ci                                    41.2s
------
 > [builder 4/7] RUN npm ci:
#12 38.91 npm ERR! code ERESOLVE
#12 38.92 npm ERR! ERESOLVE could not resolve
#12 38.92 npm ERR! While resolving: eslint-plugin-foo@3.1.0
#12 38.92 npm ERR! Found: eslint@9.4.0
#12 38.93 npm ERR! Could not resolve dependency:
#12 38.93 npm ERR! peer eslint@"^8.0.0" from eslint-plugin-foo@3.1.0

Thanks, that's clear. The build isn't broken by Docker itself. `npm ci` is refusing to install because `eslint-plugin-foo@3.1.0` wants eslint 8 and your lockfile now has eslint 9.4.0.

Two questions:
1. Did someone (or a bot like Dependabot/Renovate) merge a dependency update recently? `git log -5 -- package-lock.json` will show it.
2. Does `npm ci` fail the same way on your machine, outside Docker?

oh. yeah there's a renovate PR from last night that bumped eslint. and yes it fails locally too, I just hadn't pulled

That's the cause then. You have three ways out, from quickest to cleanest:

a) Revert the bump: `git revert <sha>` and rebuild. Fine as a stopgap.
b) Check whether the plugin has a release that supports eslint 9: `npm view eslint-plugin-foo versions --json | tail -5`. If there is one, upgrade both together.
c) If the plugin is abandoned, remove it and replace the two or three rules you actually use.

I would not use `--legacy-peer-deps` in the Dockerfile. It makes the error disappear but you end up running a plugin against an eslint version it was never tested with.

went with (b), there's a 4.0.1 that supports eslint 9. build is green again. how do I stop this from happening next time?

A few cheap guards:
- Run `npm ci` in CI on every PR, including the bot's PRs, so a broken lockfile can't be merged.
- In Renovate, group `eslint` with its plugins (`"groupName": "eslint"` plus a `matchPackagePatterns` rule) so they're bumped in one PR.
- Turn off auto-merge for major versions.

With the first one alone, last night's PR would have gone red instead of landing on main.

makes sense. added the CI step, took 5 min. thank you!
